findings.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the safeParse result object ({success, data}), and GoogleCalendarService stores that wrapper directly as credential.key, replacing the previously stored flat parsed credential object. After any token refresh, credential.key becomes {success: true, data: {...}} instead of the flat googleCredentials shape, so every subsequent consumer reading credential.key.access_token / refresh_token gets undefined and Google Calendar integration breaks after the first refresh.

[BUG] refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response in sync mode but callers were written to consume the transport-specific object (axios response or pre-parsed token), so the two shapes are silently conflated. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, every call site that dereferences the return value directly instead of passing it through a Response-handling helper reads undefined fields and writes garbage into credential.key.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, but the Google caller does res?.data, which does not exist on a Response object. With credential sync enabled, token is always undefined, googleCredentials.access_token/expiry_date are set to undefined, and the corrupted credential is persisted to the database, breaking Google Calendar for the user.

[BUG] hubspotRefreshToken is typed/used as HubspotToken (a plain object from the hubspot SDK) but in sync mode refreshOAuthTokens resolves to a fetch Response. With credential sync enabled, hubspotRefreshToken.accessToken is undefined, expiry is computed as NaN offset, and the resulting invalid key is persisted, breaking Hubspot after first refresh.

[BUG] tokenInfo comes from axios (shape {data}) in the fallback path but is a fetch Response (no .data property) in sync mode, so tokenInfo.data is undefined in sync mode. With credential sync enabled, tokenInfo.data.error is undefined so the guard passes, and the code persists access_token: undefined into the credential key, corrupting the Zoho Bigin integration.

[BUG] zohoCrmTokenInfo comes from axios ({data}) in the fallback path but is a fetch Response in sync mode, so zohoCrmTokenInfo.data is undefined in sync mode. With credential sync enabled, the !zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error guard throws 'Cannot read properties of undefined' on the sync path, crashing the Zoho CRM refresh flow.

[BUG] The computed zod object keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] evaluate to the literal string '[object Object]' at module load, not catch-all index signatures, so the schema does not implement the commented intent. In sync mode the schema only validates a property literally named '[object Object]'; any real expiry field (e.g. expiry_date) is not type-checked, and unknown properties are stripped by zod default behavior rather than allowed, contradicting the 'Assume any property with a number is the expiry' / 'Allow other properties' comments.

[ADVISORY] A new unconditional network POST to https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token is added inside the constructor/factory path that runs whenever a Salesforce connection object is created, not only when a token is actually expired. Every instantiation of SalesforceCalendarService (including non-expired credentials and read-only checks) now pays a remote token-refresh round trip plus a prisma write, adding latency and burning Salesforce refresh-token/RateLimit budget on hot paths.

[ADVISORY] Salesforce is wired to parseRefreshTokenResponse but bypasses refreshOAuthTokens, so when CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set Salesforce still refreshes with its own local client secrets and never uses the sync endpoint, unlike every other app in this diff. Self-hosters running the credential-sync deployment get inconsistent behavior: Salesforce credentials refresh locally with keys the child deployment may not have (client secrets unset -> consumer_key/client_secret empty strings -> Salesforce returns 400 on every refresh), breaking Salesforce only in the sync configuration this PR introduces.

[ADVISORY] req.headers keys are lowercased by Next.js/Node, so a CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME value containing uppercase characters (e.g. 'Calcom-Webhook-Secret') never matches any incoming header. An operator following the .env.example convention of capitalized env values sets an uppercase header name and every webhook request is rejected with 403 'Invalid webhook secret' with no hint that the value must be lowercase beyond a comment.

[ADVISORY] symmetricDecrypt is called with process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "", and decrypting with an empty key string will throw (or return garbage that JSON.parse throws on), converting a misconfiguration into an unhandled 500. A self-hoster who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET but forgets CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY gets a 500 with no diagnostic, instead of a 4xx/703-style config error identifying the missing variable.

[ADVISORY] Replacing appConfig.slug with the hardcoded string 'zoho-bigin' in the redirectUri leaves the appConfig import with a single remaining use, and the file now duplicates the slug literal that appConfig.slug provided. The next slug change or copy of this file for a sibling Zoho app must update a magic string in addition to config.json, and the partially-used appConfig import invites lint/linter-drift churn.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is typed as the truthy string/undefined result of an env check rather than a boolean, so every consumer site relies on implicit truthiness of two concatenated env values. Setting CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET to an empty string in .env.example's default ('') is correctly falsy, but any whitespace-filled or '0' value silently enables credential sharing with a bogus secret, gating a security-sensitive feature on an unvalidated string rather than an explicit flag.

[BUG] The catch-all schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property names "String" and "optional?" at module load, so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a numeric field literally named "String" and never implements the intended 'any number is the expiry' / 'allow other properties' behavior. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, every real token response (which has access_token and expiry fields but no field named "String") fails safeParse, so parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' and all OAuth token refreshes for google-calendar, office365-calendar, and zoom fail in shared-credential deployments.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), but the Google CalendarService assigns that wrapper directly as the stored credential key (`data: { key }`) instead of `key.data`. After any token refresh, credential.key is persisted as {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google credential shape, so every subsequent Google API call reading key.access_token/key.expiry_date gets undefined and calendar sync breaks for that user.

[BUG] In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but each caller expects the shape of its original refresh call (google expects a gaxios result with .data, hubspot expects a HubspotToken object, zoho-bigin/zohocrm expect an axios response with .data). With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set: google crashes on `res?.data` being undefined then `token.access_token` throwing TypeError; hubspot reads .accessToken off a Response object and persists garbage credentials; zoho-bigin and zohocrm dereference `tokenInfo.data` which is undefined on a fetch Response, throwing TypeError on every refresh — calendar/video booking flows fail for all users on self-hosted shared-credential installs.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response but the code treats it as HubspotToken, reading expiry/token fields off it. Every HubSpot token refresh under credential sharing persists undefined tokens, breaking HubSpot calendar writes silently on the next booking.

[BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while the code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` (an axios-only property), so `.data` is undefined. `!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError on every Zoho CRM credential refresh when credential sharing is enabled, failing bookings that need Zoho CRM sync.

[BUG] A Salesforce token-refresh POST plus prisma.credential.update was added to run unconditionally on every service construction, before any API call is made. Every calendar availability check/booking that instantiates SalesforceCalendarService now makes a synchronous round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write, multiplying token-endpoint load and rotating access tokens on read-only paths; a transient Salesforce failure turns reads (free-busy lookup) into 400 errors.

[BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError instead of returning a 4xx, and the decrypted `keys` payload is JSON.parse'd and written to the Credential table with no schema validation. A malformed or badly-encrypted request body produces an unhandled 500 instead of 400, and any arbitrary JSON (wrong shape, non-credential data) from a valid-secret caller is stored verbatim as credential.key, corrupting the app integration on next use.

[ADVISORY] When the sync endpoint returns only an access_token (as its own comment says: 'The response should only contain the access token and expiry date'), the code fabricates `refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, a fake literal that is then persisted as the credential's refresh token. In mixed deployments where sharing is later disabled or a caller falls back to the real refresh path, the stored fake refresh_token is sent to the provider and the credential is permanently unusable until manual re-auth; the sentinel value is indistinguishable from a real token in the DB.

[ADVISORY] New unauthenticated-by-default network endpoint implementing crypto, user lookup, upsert-or-create logic, and error handling has no tests anywhere in the diff, and the new modules parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and refreshOAuthTokens.ts (the branching heart of the feature) are likewise untested. The security-sensitive webhook path (secret comparison, decryption, DB writes) and the refresh branching can regress silently; any of the shape-mismatch bugs above would have been caught by a single test exercising each branch.

[ADVISORY] salesforceTokenSchema is defined locally in CalendarService while every other app relies on parseRefreshTokenResponse's shared minimum schema — a parallel hand-maintained token shape. When Salesforce changes its token response (e.g. adds fields, changes issued_at format), the drift between this schema and the shared minimum schema means the sharing and non-sharing paths validate differently; the next app integrated will copy this local-schema pattern instead of the shared one.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as the raw env string (`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && ...`), not a boolean, diverging from sibling constants like IS_MAILHOG_ENABLED that coerce with `=== "1"`. Callers typing it as boolean get a type error or rely on truthy-string semantics; setting the env var to "false" or "0" silently enables credential sharing, the opposite of what an operator setting CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED=false would expect.

[ADVISORY] The zod failure logging (console.error with tokenResponse.error and the raw MS response) was deleted when parseRefreshTokenResponse was introduced, and the new helper throws instead of returning the failure details. When Office365 refresh validation fails, operators lose the diagnostic output that previously identified which field the provider changed, turning a debuggable outage into an opaque 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' error.

[ADVISORY] Unrelated scope drift: the redirectUri construction is changed from appConfig.slug to a hardcoded 'zoho-bigin' string, work not traceable to the credential-sync intent. Any future slug rename or fork of this app silently diverges from appConfig.slug; the next change to config.json no longer propagates, and reviewers of sync PRs must audit drive-by edits across every app file.

[ADVISORY] New unconditional Salesforce token refresh added in this diff is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, so it is implementation work beyond the stated sync feature and a hot-path regression. Every Salesforce calendar operation (bookings, availability checks) that constructs the service now performs a blocking POST to login.salesforce.com before it did any useful work, adding latency and Salesforce API-rate-limit consumption on a path previously served from stored credentials.

[ADVISORY] Diff removes the zod-error logging on refresh-token parse failure and drops the tokenResponse.success check, an unexplained behavior change bundled into the sync PR. When Microsoft returns an unexpected token payload, the code previously logged the MS response and continued; now the failure mode is silent persistence of a malformed credential, and an operator debugging a broken Outlook integration loses the diagnostic that used to be printed.

[BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string expression, not a boolean, so CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET="" or "0" still evaluates truthy when the key exists... in practice empty string is falsy but any placeholder like 'unset' or '0' enables the feature. A self-hoster who pastes a placeholder value into .env for the paired encryption key silently enables credential sharing with a known/weak secret, causing the webhook endpoint and the sync-endpoint fetch path in every refresh call to activate unintentionally.

[BUG] The sync-mode response is returned raw with no check of HTTP status or shape, and callers that expect a typed SDK response (hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken returns HubspotToken, lark resp is a fetch Response handled by handleLarkError) receive the sync-endpoint payload instead — the integration is only half-wired per app. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED on, a HubSpot token refresh feeds whatever JSON the sync endpoint returns into hubspotClient token handling, crashing or storing garbage credentials; the diff wires refreshOAuthTokens into 8 apps but only validates the response for zoom/o365/google, so most apps are under-scoped against the stated intent.

[ADVISORY] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.string().toString() as a catch-all numeric catch-unknown key, a mechanism that does not do what the comment claims ('any property with a number is the expiry') and silently strips all other fields in sync mode. In sync mode every refreshed credential is reduced to access_token plus one arbitrary numeric field, dropping refresh_token, scope, and instance_url that the per-app schemas existed to preserve; the stored credential key loses fields the per-app code later reads (e.g. Salesforce instance_url), producing runtime failures the non-sync path does not have.

[ADVISORY] Injecting the literal string 'refresh_token' as a placeholder refresh token writes a fake secret into stored credentials, an untraceable behavior with no stated requirement behind it. Downstream code and operators see a credential that appears to hold a refresh_token but cannot be refreshed with it, turning future token-expiry failures into confusing dead ends after a sync-mode refresh.

[BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers consume it with the shape of their original client (axios `.data`, google-auth `.res.data`, hubspot SDK token object), so every field they read is undefined. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, zoho-bigin/zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data` (undefined → `!undefined.error` is true, so garbage/undefined tokens get persisted), hubspot reads `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`/`expires_in` (undefined → NaN expiry persisted), and calendar refresh silently writes broken credentials instead of falling back to the local refresh function.

[BUG] zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id) as the `userId` argument of refreshOAuthTokens, unlike every other call site which passes `credential.userId`. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint receives calcomUserId=<credential.id> and returns the parent-app credentials of the wrong user (or none), so Bigin calendars for that user get another user's tokens or a non-existent user lookup — a cross-user credential mixup path.

[BUG] In sync mode the Google refresh path assigns `res?.data` where res is the raw fetch Response from refreshOAuthTokens, so token.access_token and token.expiry_date are both undefined. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, every Google Calendar token refresh writes access_token=undefined/expiry_date=undefined (or throws at the subsequent parseRefreshTokenResponse because access_token is undefined), breaking Google Calendar sync entirely whenever credential sharing is on.

[BUG] When the synced response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the credential's key blob, overwriting the real refresh token persisted by prisma.credential.update. The stored refresh_token is destroyed and replaced with the constant "refresh_token"; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset (or a code path refreshes locally, e.g. salesforce which always refreshes locally), the next local refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and permanently fails, requiring re-authorization for every affected user.

[BUG] Salesforce was given a hand-rolled refresh fetch instead of being routed through refreshOAuthTokens, so in credential-sharing mode it still refreshes locally with its own refresh_token (which the webhook/placeholder flow may have set to "refresh_token"). Salesforce silently bypasses the central sync architecture this PR establishes: on a shared/self-hosted deployment with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Salesforce credentials drift from the parent application and break once their stored refresh_token is the placeholder, with no path through the sync endpoint to recover.

[BUG] The comment says the key 'must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm' but instructs generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which yields a 24-byte key. Self-hosters following the example produce a 24-byte key; symmetricDecrypt with a 24-byte key cannot perform AES-256, so the webhook handler throws on every sync request (or the two sides silently derive different keys), making the advertised credential sync fail at setup.

[BUG] The response check uses `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of response.ok, and fetch's statusText is commonly an empty string (e.g. HTTP/2), so successful refreshes throw a 400 HttpError. On HTTP/2 responses (or any server whose statusText is not exactly "OK") a valid token refresh throws, so Salesforce calendar operations fail even though the token endpoint succeeded.

[BUG] The computed index keys `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]` do not create a catch-all index signature — they evaluate to a single static string key at module load, so the comment 'Assume that any property with a number is the expiry' describes behavior the schema does not implement. In sync mode the parsed data contains only access_token (plus one junk literal key); every other property (expiry, scope, instance_url for salesforce) is silently stripped, so callers relying on those fields in `tokenResponse.data` get undefined and the schema's advertised permissiveness is an illusion.

[ADVISORY] The findFirst-then-update/create sequence is a check-then-insert with no unique constraint on (userId, appId) backing it. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user+app both see no existing credential and both insert, leaving duplicate Credential rows; downstream code that does findFirst will pick one arbitrarily and the other becomes unreachable stale credentials.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys are JSON.parse'd and written to Credential.key with no schema validation, unlike every other credential write path which parses through an app-specific zod schema. A partially-synced or wrongly-shaped payload from the parent application is persisted verbatim; the failure surfaces later at booking time inside the app's service class, far from the write that caused it, and with no validation error pointing at the sync endpoint.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as a truthy string (the && of two env strings), not a normalized boolean, so its type leaks `string | undefined` into every consumer's boolean checks. The next consumer that does something like `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED === true)` or stores it in a boolean-typed config gets a type error or silent falsy comparison; every current call site is silently coupled to env-string truthiness that a rename or defaulting change will break.

[ADVISORY] The Office365 refresh previously logged a zod parse failure and proceeded with the stale credentials; the new parseRefreshTokenResponse path throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' on any parse failure, changing the failure semantics for existing behavior. A single malformed provider token response now throws out of refreshAccessToken where before it degraded to the old token and logged, converting previously-survivable transient provider errors into hard booking-path failures for Outlook users.

[ADVISORY] The sync-mode fetch has no timeout, status check, or error handling, and the endpoint URL/env-var gating is duplicated as the same two-condition check in both refreshOAuthTokens and parseRefreshTokenResponse. When the sync endpoint is slow or down, every calendar operation hangs on an unbounded fetch (calendar reads are on the booking hot path); and the `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` pair is hand-maintained in multiple files, so the next sync-aware call site can easily enable only one half of the mode.

[ADVISORY] New non-trivial sync/refresh logic (refreshOAuthTokens contract, parseRefreshTokenResponse placeholder behavior, the webhook handler's create/update branching) ships with no tests anywhere in the diff. The exact failure modes above (Response-shape mismatches, placeholder refresh_token, wrong-user sync) are precisely the regressions no existing suite would catch, and each deployment with credential sharing enabled hits them on the first token expiry.

[BUG] Review iteration silently changed what gets persisted: `key` passed to prisma.credential.update is now the SafeParseReturn wrapper object from parseRefreshTokenResponse (shape {success, data, error}) instead of the previously-stored parsed credential object from googleCredentialSchema.parse(). After any token refresh with credential sharing enabled, credential.key in the DB becomes {success:true,data:...} instead of the credential payload; every consumer that reads key.access_token / key.expiry_date (CalendarService itself on next invocation, booking flows) reads undefined and Google Calendar sync breaks for refreshed users.

[BUG] The credential-sync feature was silently widened into always-on behavior: a proactive token refresh fetch to login.salesforce.com plus a prisma.credential.update now runs on every getConnection() for all users, even when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is false — this refresh path did not exist before the review iterations. Every self-hosted Salesforce user gets an extra outbound POST and a DB write on each connection construction (per booking/event check), and if the fetch or the new salesforceTokenSchema parse fails, calendar connections that previously worked (jsforce refreshes tokens itself) now hard-fail with a 400 HttpError.

[BUG] The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch is unreachable: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' when safeParse fails, so it never returns an unsuccessful result. Dead error-handling branch implies graceful rejection but the actual failure mode is an unhandled throw inside getConnection, so callers see an opaque 500 rather than the intended rejected promise path; the code was iterated into a state where the guard no longer matches the helper's contract.

[BUG] Review iterations silently deleted the error diagnostics: the console.error logging of the zod error and MS response on failed token parse was removed while the parse itself was replaced with a helper that swallows the failure shape. When Microsoft returns a malformed token response, refresh now silently persists stale/partial credentials with no log line, so operators debugging failed Outlook sync have no signal — an objective (observability of refresh failures) changed without acceptance.

[BUG] The helper fabricates a literal 'refresh_token' placeholder string and callers persist it to the DB whenever the (loose) minimumTokenResponseSchema response lacks refresh_token, changing the stored credential schema. With credential sharing enabled, the sync endpoint's response (access_token + expiry only) causes every refreshed credential in Google/O365/Zoom paths to have key.refresh_token overwritten with the fake string 'refresh_token'; if sync is later disabled, all those credentials attempt to refresh with a junk refresh token and permanently fail, requiring re-auth.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy-string derived from two independent env vars, not a declared boolean, and gate logic is duplicated across three files with slightly different conditions (webhook handler gates only on the flag, refreshOAuthTokens also requires CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT and userId, parseRefreshTokenResponse requires the endpoint). A self-hoster who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET + encryption key but no sync endpoint gets the ingest webhook active while refresh paths still use provider refresh — a half-enabled mixed state that is hard to reason about; the next app wired to this feature must remember to replicate the three-part condition correctly.

[ADVISORY] An unrelated behavioral edit (redirectUri switched from appConfig.slug interpolation to a hardcoded '/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback') rides along in a diff whose stated intent is credential sync, coupling an unrelated change to the feature PR. Behavior is currently identical, but the two copies of the slug (config.json vs string literal) can drift on rename, and reviewers auditing intent must now assess an unexplained edit inside a credential-sync PR.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's catch-all keys are computed from z.string().toString() (which does not produce a wildcard/passthrough key), so unknown properties like refresh_token are stripped from the parsed output, and the function then writes the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token, which callers persist to the credential record. The first credential-sync refresh overwrites the user's real OAuth refresh token in the DB with the placeholder string "refresh_token"; every subsequent real-provider refresh fails permanently, silently breaking the user's calendar/video integration until manual re-auth. Callers (GoogleCalendarService.ts, Office365CalendarService.ts, zoom VideoApiAdapter.ts) all write the returned object straight into prisma.credential.update.

[BUG] When credential sharing is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but this code reads res?.data as if it were the googleapis token response, so token is undefined and token.access_token throws a TypeError. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED on, every Google Calendar token refresh throws instead of refreshing, so all Google Calendar integrations fail once the cached access token expires; the catch block then persists stale credentials (or the calendar calls fail outright).

[ADVISORY] The webhook secret is compared with !== (not a constant-time comparison such as crypto.timingSafeEqual), and this single shared static secret is the only authorization for writing credentials to any user. A party holding the shared secret (which the .env.example design explicitly distributes to the external Cal.com instance) can also recover it byte-by-byte via timing side channels over many requests, gaining the ability to plant attacker-controlled credentials for arbitrary userIds.

[ADVISORY] The decrypted keys payload is JSON.parse'd and written directly into credential.key with no schema validation, and the handler performs no check that the caller is authorized for the target userId beyond the shared secret. Any holder of the webhook secret can overwrite any user's credentials for any installed app with arbitrary attacker-chosen values (e.g. an attacker-controlled calendar endpoint), exfiltrating event data or hijacking the integration; nothing validates the keys match appMetadata's credential schema.

[ADVISORY] The header lookup uses process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME verbatim against Next.js's lowercased req.headers keys, so a header-name env value containing uppercase characters never matches. An operator who sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME to any value with uppercase letters (the .env.example convention is uppercase env names, inviting exactly this) gets a permanently 403-ing endpoint — a fail-closed misconfiguration trap rather than a bypass, but it silently disables the whole sync feature.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy-string expression (process.env.A && process.env.B) rather than a boolean, so its exported value is a string or undefined, not a boolean as its name and every boolean use site implies. The next consumer that branches on it as a boolean-expected flag (e.g. serializing it into client props, or a === true check) gets surprising behavior; the change-safety cost is that every future use site must remember it is a raw string value.

[BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper, and the Google Calendar refresh path persists that wrapper object directly as the credential key, replacing the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse(...) which stored the parsed credentials. After the first token refresh with APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING disabled (the default), prisma.credential.update writes key = {success:true, data:{...}} instead of {access_token, expiry_date, refresh_token}; every subsequent Google Calendar read of credential.key (access_token/expiry_date) gets undefined, breaking all Google Calendar syncing for that credential.

[BUG] The `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` check after parseRefreshTokenResponse is dead code because parseRefreshTokenResponse itself throws ('Invalid refreshed tokens were returned') on any parse failure and only returns on success. The Promise.reject branch can never execute, and since parseRefreshTokenResponse's returned object has success=true by construction, the guard passes vacuously — a failure path the author appears to believe is covered is in fact unreachable, so any test asserting this branch's behavior would fail to exercise it as written (the throw happens earlier with a different error surface).

[ADVISORY] minimumTokenResponseSchema's 'catch-all' index signatures are computed from zod schema .toString() calls, which do not produce usable keys (e.g. '[object Object]'), so the schema is not a wildcard matcher the comment claims ('any property with a number is the expiry'). When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, token responses with extra numeric fields or unexpected shapes are validated against a schema that does not do what the code comments and callers assume; the expiry_date field the Google/Office365 paths read afterwards will be undefined, and any future test suite mocking a realistic token response would silently exercise a different schema than the code's intent.

[ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse mutates refreshTokenResponse.data to inject a sentinel refresh_token of the literal string "refresh_token", which is then persisted to the database by callers (Office365, Google, Salesforce, Zoom). A credential whose provider omits refresh_token (expected under credential sharing) gets the literal string 'refresh_token' stored as its refresh token; any code path that later falls back to non-shared mode and calls refreshOAuthTokens with this stored value will send a bogus refresh token to the provider, and the sentinel is indistinguishable from a real token so tests cannot detect the corruption without asserting exact DB content.

[BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema strips refresh_token and all non-numeric fields from the token response, and the stripped result is then persisted back into Credential.key, silently destroying the stored refresh_token. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, Google (CalendarService.ts:94-99) and O365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts) pass their full credential object through parseRefreshTokenResponse; zod's default stripping reduces it to only access_token and any numeric field, then `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token'` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal placeholder string, and the caller writes this to prisma.credential.update. The original refresh_token is irrecoverably lost — the credential can never be refreshed again outside the sync endpoint, and any credential created before the sync endpoint was configured is permanently broken. This is silent, unrecoverable data loss in the Credential.key column with no rollback path.

[BUG] The refresh_token placeholder fallback mutates and returns a credential-shaped object for non-sync paths too, where callers like Zoom expect the full parsed schema and now get a possibly mutated object. In zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts the result of parseRefreshTokenResponse is used instead of the previous zoomRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse; if the Zoom response legitimately contains refresh_token (Zoom rotates refresh tokens), the placeholder logic is a no-op, but any caller whose real schema treats refresh_token as required can no longer distinguish a genuinely missing refresh_token from the injected placeholder, and the stored credential is updated with the fake value 'refresh_token' as if it were a real token — a credential-corruption write that downstream refresh flows will use verbatim.

[ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string comparison, not a boolean flag, so '0', 'false', or 'no' all enable credential sharing. adjudication.rationale: The diff defines `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), which evaluates to a `string | undefined` (specifically the second env var’s string) and is used as a boolean gate in multiple security-sensitive paths (e.g., new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and OAuth refresh helpers). Because this gate relies on implicit truthiness of env strings, any non-empty value (including whitespace or "0") will enable the feature, without any explicit boolean flag or validation of secret strength/format, which can inadvertently enable credential sharing under weak/bogus secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The catch-all schema keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal property names "String" and "optional?" at module load, so minimumTokenResponseSchema requires a numeric field literally named "String" and never implements the intended 'any number is the expiry' / 'allow other properties' behavior. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is on, every real token response (which has access_token and expiry fields but no field named "String") fails safeParse, so parseRefreshTokenResponse throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' and all OAuth token refreshes for google-calendar, office365-calendar, and zoom fail in shared-credential deployments.
matched_golden_ids: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same underlying problem: using computed property keys like `[z.string().toString()]` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]` in a Zod object schema is invalid/misused, leading to an incorrect schema (literal property names) and runtime validation failure when parsing refresh token responses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParseReturnType wrapper ({success, data}), but the Google CalendarService assigns that wrapper directly as the stored credential key (`data: { key }`) instead of `key.data`. After any token refresh, credential.key is persisted as {success:true,data:{...}} instead of the Google credential shape, so every subsequent Google API call reading key.access_token/key.expiry_date gets undefined and calendar sync breaks for that user.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (a `{ success, data }` wrapper) and throws if `!success`, but it still returns the wrapper rather than `data`. In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refreshed credentials are parsed via `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then persisted with `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`, which would store the wrapper object instead of the Google credential shape. That would break later code expecting `credential.key.access_token` / `expiry_date`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sharing mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but each caller expects the shape of its original refresh call (google expects a gaxios result with .data, hubspot expects a HubspotToken object, zoho-bigin/zohocrm expect an axios response with .data). With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set: google crashes on `res?.data` being undefined then `token.access_token` throwing TypeError; hubspot reads .accessToken off a Response object and persists garbage credentials; zoho-bigin and zohocrm dereference `tokenInfo.data` which is undefined on a fetch Response, throwing TypeError on every refresh — calendar/video booking flows fail for all users on self-hosted shared-credential installs.
matched_golden_ids: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same core bug: when credential-sharing/sync is enabled, the refresh helper returns a raw fetch Response while callers (Google expecting res.data, Hubspot expecting a token object, etc.) assume an integration-specific token shape, causing runtime errors/invalid persistence. This matches the golden comment’s mismatch and its consequences.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response but the code treats it as HubspotToken, reading expiry/token fields off it. Every HubSpot token refresh under credential sharing persists undefined tokens, breaking HubSpot calendar writes silently on the next booking.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, it does `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response` object. But in `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the result is typed/used as `HubspotToken`: `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. In sync mode this will actually be a `Response`, so any subsequent reads of token/expiry fields from `hubspotRefreshToken` will be wrong/undefined, causing incorrect credential updates/behavior for HubSpot refresh flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response while the code reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` (an axios-only property), so `.data` is undefined. `!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError on every Zoho CRM credential refresh when credential sharing is enabled, failing bookings that need Zoho CRM sync.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff introduces `refreshOAuthTokens` which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, returns the result of `fetch(...)` (a Fetch `Response`) instead of calling the provided `refreshFunction`.

In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh path wraps an `axios(...)` call with `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then unconditionally uses axios-style access: `if (!zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error) { ... }`. In sync mode this becomes a Fetch `Response` object (no `.data`), so `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` throws a TypeError. This is directly verifiable from the shown implementations and call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A Salesforce token-refresh POST plus prisma.credential.update was added to run unconditionally on every service construction, before any API call is made. Every calendar availability check/booking that instantiates SalesforceCalendarService now makes a synchronous round-trip to login.salesforce.com and a DB write, multiplying token-endpoint load and rotating access tokens on read-only paths; a transient Salesforce failure turns reads (free-busy lookup) into 400 errors.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, a refresh-token exchange (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token" ...)`) and subsequent `prisma.credential.update(...)` were added unconditionally immediately before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no check for token expiry/need-to-refresh, so any code path that constructs/initializes the Salesforce service/connection will now always perform a network round-trip to Salesforce and a DB write even for read-only operations. Additionally, failures in that refresh call throw `HttpError` (statusCode 400), which can cause otherwise read operations to fail due to transient token endpoint issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a ZodError instead of returning a 4xx, and the decrypted `keys` payload is JSON.parse'd and written to the Credential table with no schema validation. A malformed or badly-encrypted request body produces an unhandled 500 instead of 400, and any arbitrary JSON (wrong shape, non-credential data) from a valid-secret caller is stored verbatim as credential.key, corrupting the app integration on next use.

[ADVISORY] When the sync endpoint returns only an access_token (as its own comment says: 'The response should only contain the access token and expiry date'), the code fabricates `refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, a fake literal that is then persisted as the credential's refresh token. In mixed deployments where sharing is later disabled or a caller falls back to the real refresh path, the stored fake refresh_token is sent to the provider and the credential is permanently unusable until manual re-auth; the sentinel value is indistinguishable from a real token in the DB.

[ADVISORY] New unauthenticated-by-default network endpoint implementing crypto, user lookup, upsert-or-create logic, and error handling has no tests anywhere in the diff, and the new modules parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and refreshOAuthTokens.ts (the branching heart of the feature) are likewise untested. The security-sensitive webhook path (secret comparison, decryption, DB writes) and the refresh branching can regress silently; any of the shape-mismatch bugs above would have been caught by a single test exercising each branch.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new webhook API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` that performs secret-header verification, AES decryption (`symmetricDecrypt`), user/app lookups, and credential update/create DB writes, plus new branching utilities `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts` and `refreshOAuthTokens.ts` that change token-refresh behavior across multiple integrations. The diff does not add any test files or test coverage for these new security- and correctness-sensitive branches/endpoints, so regressions (e.g., header-name handling, decrypt/JSON parse failures, branching between remote refresh vs local refresh) could slip through silently. This is a concrete, diff-grounded review gap rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] salesforceTokenSchema is defined locally in CalendarService while every other app relies on parseRefreshTokenResponse's shared minimum schema — a parallel hand-maintained token shape. When Salesforce changes its token response (e.g. adds fields, changes issued_at format), the drift between this schema and the shared minimum schema means the sharing and non-sharing paths validate differently; the next app integrated will copy this local-schema pattern instead of the shared one.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s core claim (“every other app relies on parseRefreshTokenResponse’s shared minimum schema”) is not supported by the diff: multiple integrations pass their own concrete schemas into `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (e.g., Office365 uses `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, Zoom uses `zoomRefreshedTokenSchema`, Google passes `googleCredentialSchema`). `parseRefreshTokenResponse` itself selects the shared `minimumTokenResponseSchema` only when credential sharing is enabled; otherwise it validates against the caller-provided schema. Salesforce adding a local `salesforceTokenSchema` is consistent with this pattern, and the alleged ‘drift’ is speculative rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is exported as the raw env string (`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && ...`), not a boolean, diverging from sibling constants like IS_MAILHOG_ENABLED that coerce with `=== "1"`. Callers typing it as boolean get a type error or rely on truthy-string semantics; setting the env var to "false" or "0" silently enables credential sharing, the opposite of what an operator setting CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED=false would expect.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY;`, and in JS/TS `&&` returns the last truthy operand, so this constant is inferred as `string | undefined` (not a boolean). The new code uses it as a boolean gate (e.g. `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)` in the new OAuth helpers), meaning it relies on truthy-string semantics; values like "0"/"false" are truthy and would still enable the feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The zod failure logging (console.error with tokenResponse.error and the raw MS response) was deleted when parseRefreshTokenResponse was introduced, and the new helper throws instead of returning the failure details. When Office365 refresh validation fails, operators lose the diagnostic output that previously identified which field the provider changed, turning a debuggable outage into an opaque 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' error.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`: the previous `console.error("Outlook error...", tokenResponse.error, "MS response:", responseJson)` block after `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` was removed. The new `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)` helper (added in `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`) throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when validation fails, and does not log the zod error or raw provider response. This is a real diff-grounded observability/diagnostics regression (less actionable operator output), though not necessarily a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Unrelated scope drift: the redirectUri construction is changed from appConfig.slug to a hardcoded 'zoho-bigin' string, work not traceable to the credential-sync intent. Any future slug rename or fork of this app silently diverges from appConfig.slug; the next change to config.json no longer propagates, and reviewers of sync PRs must audit drive-by edits across every app file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts` redirect URI from `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback`` to a hardcoded `WEBAPP_URL + `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback``. This is a diff-grounded maintainability/scope concern: it bypasses `appConfig.slug`, so future changes to `config.json` (e.g., slug rename/fork) would not propagate to the redirect URI. It’s not a verifiable immediate defect in this PR because the current slug may already be `zoho-bigin`, but it introduces divergence risk unrelated to the credential-sync intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] New unconditional Salesforce token refresh added in this diff is not gated on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, so it is implementation work beyond the stated sync feature and a hot-path regression. Every Salesforce calendar operation (bookings, availability checks) that constructs the service now performs a blocking POST to login.salesforce.com before it did any useful work, adding latency and Salesforce API-rate-limit consumption on a path previously served from stored credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional token refresh `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` and `prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `jsforce.Connection`, with no gating on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` or any expiry check. This means constructing the Salesforce calendar service now always performs a blocking network POST and consumes Salesforce API quota, which is a concrete performance/scope regression relative to previously using stored credentials. While not necessarily functionally incorrect, it is a significant hot-path/architecture concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Diff removes the zod-error logging on refresh-token parse failure and drops the tokenResponse.success check, an unexplained behavior change bundled into the sync PR. When Microsoft returns an unexpected token payload, the code previously logged the MS response and continued; now the failure mode is silent persistence of a malformed credential, and an operator debugging a broken Outlook integration loses the diagnostic that used to be printed.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the explicit `console.error(...)` logging on Zod parse failure is removed, but the code does not “drop the tokenResponse.success check” (it still does `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)`). More importantly, the new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` throws when `safeParse` fails, so the failure mode is not “silent persistence of a malformed credential”; execution would abort rather than continue updating Prisma with malformed data. The finding mischaracterizes the new behavior based on what the diff shows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string expression, not a boolean, so CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET="" or "0" still evaluates truthy when the key exists... in practice empty string is falsy but any placeholder like 'unset' or '0' enables the feature. A self-hoster who pastes a placeholder value into .env for the paired encryption key silently enables credential sharing with a known/weak secret, causing the webhook endpoint and the sync-endpoint fetch path in every refresh call to activate unintentionally.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which yields a string/undefined (the second operand) rather than a boolean. It’s then used as a boolean gate in multiple places (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` in `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId)` in `refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). While this still works via truthiness coercion (empty string is falsy), the finding’s concern is valid as a configuration footgun: any non-empty placeholder value (e.g. "0", "unset") would enable the feature and could result in a weak/guessable secret being accepted by the new webhook auth check. This is a design/configuration robustness issue rather than a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The sync-mode response is returned raw with no check of HTTP status or shape, and callers that expect a typed SDK response (hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken returns HubspotToken, lark resp is a fetch Response handled by handleLarkError) receive the sync-endpoint payload instead — the integration is only half-wired per app. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED on, a HubSpot token refresh feeds whatever JSON the sync endpoint returns into hubspotClient token handling, crashing or storing garbage credentials; the diff wires refreshOAuthTokens into 8 apps but only validates the response for zoom/o365/google, so most apps are under-scoped against the stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the raw `fetch(...)` result (a `Response`) without checking `response.ok` or parsing/validating JSON (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Several callers previously expected a provider SDK/axios token object and now assign the sync `Response` into those variables. Example: HubSpot refresh now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` where the non-sync branch returns a `HubspotToken` but the sync branch returns a `Response` (`packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`), so subsequent access like `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token` / token fields will break or store garbage. Similarly, Zoho BigIn and ZohoCRM wrap `axios(...)` in `refreshOAuthTokens` but would receive a `Response` (no `.data`) in sync mode (`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`). Only a few integrations add extra parsing (`parseRefreshTokenResponse`) and even those still depend on caller handling; most are half-wired as the finding claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The minimumTokenResponseSchema uses z.string().toString() as a catch-all numeric catch-unknown key, a mechanism that does not do what the comment claims ('any property with a number is the expiry') and silently strips all other fields in sync mode. In sync mode every refreshed credential is reduced to access_token plus one arbitrary numeric field, dropping refresh_token, scope, and instance_url that the per-app schemas existed to preserve; the stored credential key loses fields the per-app code later reads (e.g. Salesforce instance_url), producing runtime failures the non-sync path does not have.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is not a valid “any numeric key is expiry / allow other properties” schema: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` become literal property names (e.g. "ZodString"), and the `z.object(...)` is not `.passthrough()`, so unknown fields are stripped. In sync mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` will therefore accept and return only `access_token` plus at most that one literal numeric field, dropping fields that per-app schemas preserve (e.g., Salesforce `instance_url`, `scope`, etc.). Since refreshed credentials are persisted back into `prisma.credential.update(...)` in multiple services, this can cause stored credential keys to lose required fields and lead to runtime failures compared to the non-sync path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Injecting the literal string 'refresh_token' as a placeholder refresh token writes a fake secret into stored credentials, an untraceable behavior with no stated requirement behind it. Downstream code and operators see a credential that appears to hold a refresh_token but cannot be refreshed with it, turning future token-expiry failures into confusing dead ends after a sync-mode refresh.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `parseRefreshTokenResponse` which mutates the parsed token payload to inject a literal `refresh_token` string when the response lacks one (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`). In sync-mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` + `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), the minimal schema does not require a real refresh token, so this placeholder can propagate into persisted credentials. This is concretely harmful in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, where the parsed token data is spread into `o365AuthCredentials` (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) }`), which would overwrite a real stored refresh token with the fake placeholder, causing future refresh attempts to fail and leaving misleading stored secrets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response, but several callers consume it with the shape of their original client (axios `.data`, google-auth `.res.data`, hubspot SDK token object), so every field they read is undefined. With CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, zoho-bigin/zohocrm read `tokenInfo.data` (undefined → `!undefined.error` is true, so garbage/undefined tokens get persisted), hubspot reads `hubspotRefreshToken.refresh_token`/`expires_in` (undefined → NaN expiry persisted), and calendar refresh silently writes broken credentials instead of falling back to the local refresh function.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, the function returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response`. Multiple callers still treat the return value as their original client’s shape: e.g. Google Calendar does `const token = res?.data` (but `Response` has no `.data`), Hubspot assigns it to `HubspotToken` (but will receive `Response`), and Zoho Bigin/ZohoCRM access `tokenInfo.data.error` / `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` (will be `undefined` and/or throw). The diff shows no normalization/parsing step in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so enabling `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` will break these refresh flows at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] zoho-bigin passes `credentialId` (the Credential row id) as the `userId` argument of refreshOAuthTokens, unlike every other call site which passes `credential.userId`. With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint receives calcomUserId=<credential.id> and returns the parent-app credentials of the wrong user (or none), so Bigin calendars for that user get another user's tokens or a non-existent user lookup — a cross-user credential mixup path.
matched_golden_ids: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: `refreshOAuthTokens` is called with `credentialId` (credential row id) where `userId`/`credential.userId` is expected, leading to incorrect user lookups during credential sync and potentially syncing the wrong/no credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] In sync mode the Google refresh path assigns `res?.data` where res is the raw fetch Response from refreshOAuthTokens, so token.access_token and token.expiry_date are both undefined. With APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED, every Google Calendar token refresh writes access_token=undefined/expiry_date=undefined (or throws at the subsequent parseRefreshTokenResponse because access_token is undefined), breaking Google Calendar sync entirely whenever credential sharing is on.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data; googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token;`.

But `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` object when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). A `Response` does not have a `.data` property, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` throws (or would lead to undefined values if it didn’t throw). This breaks the Google Calendar refresh path whenever credential sharing/sync mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When the synced response has no refresh_token, the code writes the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" into the credential's key blob, overwriting the real refresh token persisted by prisma.credential.update. The stored refresh_token is destroyed and replaced with the constant "refresh_token"; if CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is later unset (or a code path refreshes locally, e.g. salesforce which always refreshes locally), the next local refresh sends refresh_token="refresh_token" and permanently fails, requiring re-authorization for every affected user.
matched_golden_ids: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate describes the same bug: when the OAuth refresh response lacks a refresh_token, the code stores the literal string "refresh_token" (a hardcoded placeholder) into persisted credentials, overwriting the real token and causing subsequent refresh/auth failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Salesforce was given a hand-rolled refresh fetch instead of being routed through refreshOAuthTokens, so in credential-sharing mode it still refreshes locally with its own refresh_token (which the webhook/placeholder flow may have set to "refresh_token"). Salesforce silently bypasses the central sync architecture this PR establishes: on a shared/self-hosted deployment with CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT set, Salesforce credentials drift from the parent application and break once their stored refresh_token is the placeholder, with no path through the sync endpoint to recover.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a central refresh path via `refreshOAuthTokens` (used by Google, Hubspot, Office365, Zoom, Webex, Zoho, etc.) when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set. However, `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` does a direct `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using `credentialKey.refresh_token` and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so Salesforce will not use the sync endpoint in credential-sharing mode. This is verifiable from the diff: Salesforce imports `parseRefreshTokenResponse` but not `refreshOAuthTokens`, and the refresh request body explicitly includes `refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token`. In sharing mode, other code paths can end up persisting a placeholder refresh token (`parseRefreshTokenResponse` sets `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when missing), so Salesforce’s local refresh can break with no fallback to the sync endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The comment says the key 'must be 32 bytes for AES256 encryption algorithm' but instructs generating it with `openssl rand -base64 24`, which yields a 24-byte key.
