adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse mutates refreshTokenResponse.data to inject a sentinel refresh_token of the literal string "refresh_token", which is then persisted to the database by callers (Office365, Google, Salesforce, Zoom). A credential whose provider omits refresh_token (expected under credential sharing) gets the literal string 'refresh_token' stored as its refresh token; any code path that later falls back to non-shared mode and calls refreshOAuthTokens with this stored value will send a bogus refresh token to the provider, and the sentinel is indistinguishable from a real token so tests cannot detect the corruption without asserting exact DB content.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function explicitly mutates the parsed result to inject a literal sentinel when the provider response omits `refresh_token`: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"; }`. Callers then persist refreshed credentials back to Prisma (e.g., Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials` and updates `prisma.credential`), which would overwrite a real refresh token with the literal string when running in the “credential sharing” mode where refresh_token may be omitted. If credential sharing is later disabled (env-based `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED`), refresh flows that use the stored refresh token would send the bogus literal to providers. This is a correctness/data-corruption issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema strips refresh_token and all non-numeric fields from the token response, and the stripped result is then persisted back into Credential.key, silently destroying the stored refresh_token. When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, Google (CalendarService.ts:94-99) and O365 (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts) pass their full credential object through parseRefreshTokenResponse; zod's default stripping reduces it to only access_token and any numeric field, then `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = 'refresh_token'` overwrites the real refresh token with the literal placeholder string, and the caller writes this to prisma.credential.update. The original refresh_token is irrecoverably lost — the credential can never be refreshed again outside the sync endpoint, and any credential created before the sync endpoint was configured is permanently broken. This is silent, unrecoverable data loss in the Credential.key column with no rollback path.

adjudication.rationale: The claimed “silent data loss” via Zod stripping/persisting isn’t verifiable from the diff because `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is not a true catch-all schema: it uses computed keys like `[z.string().toString()]`, which become a literal property name (e.g., "ZodString"), making the schema likely *fail* parsing for normal OAuth token objects rather than successfully strip fields. In that failure case, `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws (`throw new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")`), so the update path that would overwrite/persist a placeholder refresh token is not shown to occur silently. While the new helper has serious issues, the specific mechanism and outcome described (successful parse → stripping → placeholder refresh_token persisted, irrecoverable silent loss) doesn’t match what can be confirmed from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The refresh_token placeholder fallback mutates and returns a credential-shaped object for non-sync paths too, where callers like Zoom expect the full parsed schema and now get a possibly mutated object. In zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts the result of parseRefreshTokenResponse is used instead of the previous zoomRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse; if the Zoom response legitimately contains refresh_token (Zoom rotates refresh tokens), the placeholder logic is a no-op, but any caller whose real schema treats refresh_token as required can no longer distinguish a genuinely missing refresh_token from the injected placeholder, and the stored credential is updated with the fake value 'refresh_token' as if it were a real token — a credential-corruption write that downstream refresh flows will use verbatim.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, after a successful parse the code unconditionally injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) { ... }`). This behavior is not limited to the sync/minimum-schema branch; it occurs for any successful parse where `refresh_token` is absent/optional. Call sites were changed to use this helper (e.g. `packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts` now calls `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseBody, zoomRefreshedTokenSchema)`), which can mask a genuinely missing/omitted `refresh_token` and can propagate a fake refresh token value downstream (and potentially into persisted credentials, depending on the caller’s update logic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a truthy string comparison, not a boolean flag, so '0', 'false', or 'no' all enable credential sharing. Operators following the .env.example pattern of empty-string/false-style toggles who set CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET="false" (or any non-empty sentinel) silently turn on credential sharing and the remote sync endpoint path, redirecting every OAuth token refresh across google-calendar, o365, zoom, webex, lark, hubspot, and zoho to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT; every other flag in constants.ts (e.g. IS_MAILHOG_ENABLED) uses === "1", so the next change to this file will likely copy the correct pattern and the behavioral cliff remains hidden until a self-hoster debugging refresh failures finds it.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/lib/constants.ts, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which yields a truthy string (or undefined), not a boolean check like `=== "1"`. As a result, setting either env var to any non-empty sentinel (e.g., "0"/"false") will still enable the feature. This flag is then used to gate the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`) and the token refresh redirection logic (`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`), so the finding’s core claim about accidental enablement is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The Salesforce refresh now unconditionally overwrites Credential.key with the token response, dropping any extra fields (e.g. previously stored metadata) that existed in the old key object. Previously the jsforce connection refreshed tokens internally without rewriting Credential.key; now every isCacheValid miss performs a fetch plus a prisma.credential.update that replaces the whole key JSON with only the schema fields plus the old refresh_token. If the stored key carried any additional persisted fields from earlier versions of the integration, they are silently removed on the first refresh after this deploys — a same-column repurposing (full key object → narrowed token object) with no backup of the prior value.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh logic does `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }}})`, where `accessTokenParsed.data` is constrained to `salesforceTokenSchema` (id, issued_at, instance_url, signature, access_token, scope, token_type). This overwrites the entire `Credential.key` JSON, preserving only those fields plus the old `refresh_token`, thereby dropping any other previously persisted fields that may have existed in `credential.key` (e.g., additional metadata). That is verifiable from the diff and constitutes potential silent data loss on refresh.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] minimumTokenResponseSchema's computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to the literal string "[object Object]" at runtime, so the schema only validates access_token and zod strips every other property (including expiry_date) from the parsed output. Whenever credential sharing is enabled, every caller of parseRefreshTokenResponse (zoom, office365-calendar, salesforce) receives data containing only {access_token}; the expiry is silently dropped and a literal placeholder refresh_token = "refresh_token" is written into the credential row, permanently destroying the real refresh_token and forcing a re-auth or breaking future refreshes with no error surfaced.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. Those expressions evaluate to a single literal property name at runtime (not a dynamic “any string key”/index signature), so the schema effectively validates only `access_token` (and possibly one weird literal key) and Zod will strip real fields like `expiry_date`/`expires_in`/`refresh_token` from `data`. When the “minimum” path is used (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` then sees no `refresh_token` and force-sets `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"`, which can overwrite the real refresh token when callers merge/store `tokenResponse.data` (e.g. Office365 refresh flow now merges `tokenResponse.data` into `o365AuthCredentials`). This is data-loss/broken refresh behavior introduced by the diff. (Salesforce avoids this by explicitly reusing the old refresh_token, but others do not.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The refresh handler stores the entire safeParse wrapper object (`{success, data, error}` returned by parseRefreshTokenResponse) as the credential key instead of the parsed data, replacing the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the data itself. prisma.credential.update writes `{success: true, data: {...}}` into credential.key; on the next use, googleCredentials.access_token is undefined and the Google calendar integration fails for that user until the credential is manually repaired, while the refresh itself returned success.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and persists it via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. But `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (new file) returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (i.e., `{ success, data, error }`), not the parsed credential data. This replaces the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)` which returned the data itself. Storing the wrapper object in `credential.key` would break later usage where code expects `credential.key` to directly contain fields like `access_token`/`refresh_token`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response object, and the code then reads `res?.data` — a property that does not exist on a fetch Response — so token is undefined. `token.access_token` throws TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined) inside refreshAccessToken, turning a refresh under credential-sharing mode into an unhandled 500 on the booking path instead of a token refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, it performs `fetch(...)` and returns that raw `Response` object. But callers (e.g. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`) treat the return value like an axios/google client response: `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...); const token = res?.data;` and then use `token.access_token`. A `fetch` `Response` has no `.data`, so `token` becomes `undefined` and `token.access_token` will throw at runtime when credential sync mode is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response but the result is assigned directly to hubspotRefreshToken and consumed as a HubspotToken object, so refreshToken/accessToken are undefined on this path. The service computes expiry from an undefined timestamp and persists a credential whose token fields are undefined, reporting a successful refresh while storing a broken credential that fails all subsequent Hubspot API calls.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when credential sync is enabled it does `return response;` where `response` is the raw `fetch(...)` Response object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` assumes the returned value is a `HubspotToken` (the old behavior of `hubspotClient.oauth.tokensApi.createToken(...)`). On the sync-enabled path, `hubspotRefreshToken` will instead be a `Response`, so token fields (e.g., access/refresh/expiry-related fields) will be undefined and any subsequent expiry computation / credential persistence will be wrong. The diff shows no JSON parsing of the Response in the hubspot code path, making this a verifiable correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response whose `.data` property is undefined, and line 97 immediately reads `tokenInfo.data.error`. TypeError (Cannot read properties of undefined reading 'error') on every token refresh under sync mode, crashing the calendar operation with a 500 instead of refreshing the token.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `refreshOAuthTokens` (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) which, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is truthy, executes `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns the raw Fetch `Response`. Multiple callers (e.g. packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts) treat the return value as an Axios response (`tokenInfo.data.error`). A Fetch `Response` does not have a `.data` property, so under sync mode `tokenInfo.data` is `undefined` and accessing `.error` will throw. This matches the reported crash scenario (TypeError) and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] With credential sync enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response and the code then reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error` on an object that has no `.data`. TypeError on every refresh under sync mode, a raw 500 on the booking path instead of a token refresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`, the function performs a `fetch(...)` and returns the raw `Response`. In `packages/app-store/zohocrm/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the caller assigns `const zohoCrmTokenInfo = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then immediately reads `zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error`, which is an Axios response shape. Under sync mode this will be a Fetch `Response` (no `.data`), causing a TypeError and a 500 during token refresh. This mismatch is directly introduced by the diff and is reproducible from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The webhook secret header lookup uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` without lowercasing the configured header name, but Node.js lowercases all incoming header keys. If an operator sets CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME to any mixed-case value (e.g. the documented style "Calcom-Webhook-Secret"), req.headers never contains that key and every webhook request is rejected with 403, making the entire credential-sync feature silently non-functional.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check indexes `req.headers` with `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` verbatim: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]`. The diff contains no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`). Since the header name is configurable, any mixed/upper-case value would not match the typical lowercased keys in Node/Next request headers, causing the comparison to fail and return 403 for otherwise valid requests. (The added .env comment advises lowercase, but the code still makes the feature fragile to configuration.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws an unhandled ZodError on malformed payloads, and lines 60-63 symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse likewise throw unguarded on a bad ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext. A caller posting an invalid body (or a sender with a mismatched encryption key) receives a raw 500 from the Next.js API instead of the 4xx validation error the handler otherwise promises, so the sender cannot distinguish 'bad payload' from 'server failure' and retries blindly.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags that `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` can throw an unhandled ZodError on malformed payloads, resulting in a 500 response instead of the intended 4xx (e.g., 400) validation error. This is the same core issue as the golden comment, though the candidate also adds related unguarded throws in decryption/JSON parsing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] A Salesforce token refresh (remote fetch plus a prisma.credential.update) now runs unconditionally inside the service constructor/connection setup path on every instantiation, with no expiry check, caching, or in-flight guard. Every calendar operation that constructs SalesforceCalendarService issues a full token refresh and a DB write, multiplying remote calls per process and per request; concurrent operations race on the same credential row and hammer login.salesforce.com, risking refresh-token rotation invalidating in-flight copies.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token exchange and DB write on the service setup path: it immediately `fetch`es `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` using `credentialKey.refresh_token`, then `await prisma.credential.update(...)` before returning the `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no expiry check, memoization, or concurrency guard shown, so every instantiation of `SalesforceCalendarService` will perform a remote refresh and update the credential row, which can amplify calls and introduce races on the same credential under concurrent operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The fetch to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT on the token-refresh request path has no timeout, no response.ok/status check, and no payload-size bound. If the sync endpoint hangs, every booking involving a shared credential stalls indefinitely (all callers await this promise with no AbortController); if it returns a non-JSON error page, downstream parsers throw an unrelated 500, masking the real failure.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it does `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams(...) })` and immediately returns the `response` without any timeout/AbortController, without checking `response.ok`/status, and without guarding/parsing the body. Callers then treat the returned value as if it were a normal token-refresh response (e.g., `Office365CalendarService` passes it to `handleErrorsJson(response)` which will attempt to parse JSON; `GoogleCalendarService` expects `res?.data`). A hanging sync endpoint will stall awaiting callers indefinitely, and non-JSON error bodies will surface as generic parsing/500 errors, masking the real upstream failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The findFirst-then-update/create sequence is not atomic, and the writes store the raw JSON.parse output as the credential key with no schema validation. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app create duplicate credential rows (the 'Can't use upsert' comment acknowledges the race but the shipped code still loses it), and a payload decrypting to a non-object stores a structurally invalid credential that fails at first use, long after the webhook returned 200 success.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts and `JSON.parse`s `reqBody.keys` and then writes it directly to `credential.key` (`data: { key: keys }`) without any schema validation. Since `zod` only validates `keys` is a string, a decrypted payload that parses to a non-object (or wrong shape) will still be persisted and the webhook will return 200, potentially causing failures later when the credential is used. Additionally, the `findFirst`-then-`update`/`create` sequence is not atomic; two concurrent requests for the same `userId`/`appId` can both miss the existing row and both create, unless there is an unseen DB uniqueness constraint (not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] parseRefreshTokenResponse overwrites a missing refresh_token with the literal placeholder string "refresh_token" before the credential is persisted. Any integration whose refresh response legitimately omits refresh_token gets a fake refresh_token persisted, so the next real refresh attempts to use the string 'refresh_token' as an OAuth grant and fails — the placeholder should flow through the sync path only, not be written into stored credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function mutates the parsed token payload by setting `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` whenever it is missing. Call sites can then persist this value: e.g. `Office365CalendarService` does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` after calling `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, so if the refresh response omits `refresh_token`, the placeholder overwrites the real stored refresh token and will be written back to Prisma in the subsequent `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This can break subsequent refreshes by using the literal string "refresh_token" as the grant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The check `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` after parseRefreshTokenResponse is dead code, because parseRefreshTokenResponse already throws on failure; the Promise.reject branch can never execute. Not a behavior bug today, but it misleads readers into thinking there is a non-throwing failure path here; when someone later 'simplifies' parseRefreshTokenResponse to return results instead of throwing, this path silently becomes the only guard — and the mixed success-check/throw contract across callers (zoom checks .success, google uses .data directly) is itself a drift hazard.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the function throws when `safeParse` fails (`if (!refreshTokenResponse.success) { throw new Error(...) }`) and otherwise returns a successful Zod result. In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the subsequent guard `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) { return Promise.reject(...) }` is therefore unreachable dead code. This isn’t a runtime defect today, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability issue and highlights an inconsistent caller contract (some callers treat the return as always-success/throwing, while others still check `.success`).
